results.title: Meta-analytic factor analysis of the UCLA loneliness scale | Current Psychology
results.content: Hence, this study employs meta-analytical structural equation modeling (MASEM) to investigate the factor structure of the UCLA Loneliness Scale, MASEM provides more precise parameter estimations than conventional structural equation modeling and allows for the synthesis of conflicting findings concerning factor structure. In this study, the factor analysis model was tested within the framework of MASEM by making efforts to obtain correlation matrices from each of the primary study authors. Which of the single-factor, two-factor, and second-order three-factor models provided the best fit to the pooled correlation matrices in the subgroups formed according to the moderator variables of sample size and sample age? The primary studies included in this meta-analysis underwent evaluation according to the following criteria: Adherence to the inclusion criteria for meta-analysis, employing of the PRISMA flowchart to enhance transparency in the study inclusion process, examining the adequacy of the sample size (studies with very small sample sizes were excluded as seen in the PRISMA flowchart), checking the reported reliability and validity values of the ULS used in the studies, being very careful to access the data accurately in the process of obtaining the correlation matrices required for the effect size from the authors. The pooled correlation matrix estimated according to the GLS and TSSEM methods was first tested with the single-factor CFA model in the second stage of MASEM. For this purpose, the correlation matrices in the primary studies using the ULS were collected, and the meta-analytic CFA analysis of the single-factor, two-factor, and second-order three-factor model was carried out, taking into account the studies on the factor structure of the scale in the literature (Durak & Senol-Durak, 2010. In the structural validity study conducted in the Turkish sample, it was seen that the second-order three-factor model with the *global* loneliness factor and the two-factor model were more compatible with the data (Durak & Senol-Durak, 2010. The fact that the sample size was large enough and the missing correlation values were not included in the analyses carried out with all data in this study might have ensured that there were no major differences between the correlation matrices pooled according to the GLS and TSSEM methods, consistent with the information in the literature.

results.title: (PDF) Permutational tests for correlation matrices
results.content: In this article we show that the Kullback's statistic for testing equality of several correlation matrices may be considered a modified likelihood ratio statistic when sampling from multivariate normal populations. We propose a permutation test to approximate the distribution of a new test statistic, which represents a generalization of the intra-cluster correlation in regression models with one variance component. The paper proposes a permutational procedure for testing equality of eigenvectors in population correlation matrices, addressing limitations of existing likelihood ratio tests.
